task: 468 dense 3D face landmarks + a presence score (MediaPipe Face Mesh V1). Not a detection/classification model - ground truth here is geometric (do the landmarks land on the actual detected face region) and structural (right shape/dtype/finiteness), not a class label.
note:
Real gate-2 shape independently re-confirmed this session: input 'input' (batch,3,192,192) float32, outputs 'landmarks' (batch,468,3) float32 and 'score' (batch,1) float32 - matches CHECKLIST.md's prior write-up and MediaPipe's own public, stable 468-point spec exactly.

Only fixture in this repo with usable real faces (see uniface-adaface-recognition/manifest.json for the full explanation). The production SCRFD face detector found 2 of the 3 visible real faces; this model runs once per detected face, cropped via uniface's own MediaPipe-matching ROI recipe (a square region 1.5x the detector box, rolled level using the detector's own eye keypoints - ported from uniface.landmark.facemesh.roi_from_box/warp_roi, github.com/yakhyo/uniface, cross-checked line-for-line against the real clone in this repo's uniface-main/ this session).

**What 'ground truth' means for a dense landmark model without a labelled 468-point reference for this specific image**: rather than fabricate per-point coordinates (which would be a guess dressed up as ground truth - exactly what this project's own discipline forbids), this manifest checks the property that IS independently verifiable from the detector's own already-verified output: do the returned 2D landmark coordinates fall within (or very close to) the SAME face region the production SCRFD detector itself reported for that face. A facemesh whose coordinate transform is wrong (e.g. a sign error in the inverse-affine mapping, or a stale ROI) would produce landmarks nowhere near the detector's own box - that failure mode IS caught by this check, even without a full 468-point reference.

expected.landmarks_fall_within_detector_bbox_regi: x/y ranges should sit inside (or very close to) each face's own SCRFD bbox, not somewhere else in the frame or wildly out of the 0..width/0..height range
